title: Restore a robot vacuum caster seized by wound fibres
instruction: Restore free movement of the robot vacuum caster.
justification: Actual robot locomotion maintenance documented by manufacturer, with original full-size hardware.
fault: Wrapped hair/fibre mat physically restricts wheel/axle rotation.
objects: Powered-off340x340x94mm3.4kg Roomba i7 inverted on native bench
Original25.4g front caster module, rounded26x18mm wheel, removable axle and stem
Physical wound fibre mat and ordinary loose parts tray
skill: Service small original captive wheel/axle mechanism, clear compressed wound fibres and reinstall original parts while preserving free wheel/swivel motion.
scoring: Not implemented; full score must require released reassembled original caster, all fibres outside bearing/axle region and measured physical free rotation. Initial diagnostic scores remain0.

nearest.difference: Brush refit, rejected for bare block/roller fixture and nonphysical retainer. Must model actual whole unit, yoke/axle retention and hair drag.
i7brush-door opening alone rejected as hidden partial maintenance; caster task must finish recovery, not stop at removal.
Robot bin removal, hold-release dumping and reinsert; does not disassemble axle or clear wound obstruction.
Circlip pliers retaining-ring installation on loose shaft; retention alone is already covered. Its loose support requirement rules out silently anchoring the vacuum.
Root-owned Roborock keyed brush and hooked cover recovery. Caster distinction must be physical wound-fibre clearance plus free axle/swivel restoration, not change of vacuum part.

risks: Hair-mat effective compliance/friction is not calibrated OEM data; native small-scale contact may be unstable.
Real yoke and stem retention compliance must be physically represented without inventing access or event locks.
Actual axle pushout and mat handling may be less accessible than wheel grip.
Source-backed geometrical reconstruction and full-unit recognizability need visual review.
state: held after two bounded native gate failures; no full repair
